_about: Hand-annotated ground truth for the position/distance accuracy test (v2 set).
Each entry was written by looking at the image and recording where a human
perceives the object to be, independently of what the detector outputs.
Sources of the 10 scenes:
vid_XXs.jpg  - real frames extracted from the 60 s webcam recording
(assets/scene60.avi), timestamps 3/11/19/27/35/43/51 s
sample_*.jpg - the three sample photos, annotations carried over unchanged
from the original ground_truth.json (verified in the v1 report)
The original 7 webcam frames (cam_01..cam_07.jpg) referenced by the v1 set
are no longer on disk; only their annotated copies survive in
Evidence/eval_position/. This v2 set replaces them with freshly recorded
real frames so the 10-scene test can be re-run.
Fields per object:
label        - COCO class name (must be inside the app's default whitelist)
cx_frac      - HUMAN estimate of the object's centre-x as a fraction of the
frame width (0.0 = left edge, 1.0 = right edge). Used only
to pair expectations with detections, never to score them.
horizontal   - 'left' / 'ahead' / 'right', judged by eye
distance_band- 'very close' / 'near' / 'far', judged by apparent size
Direction rule (the same three-way split the app implements):
centre_x < width/3      -> left
centre_x < 2*width/3    -> ahead
otherwise               -> right
Distance bands are judged from how much of the frame the object appears to
occupy (the same cue the app uses, but judged by eye, not computed):
>= 20% of frame -> 'very close', >= 5% -> 'near', else 'far'.
This is deliberately NOT ground-truth depth: there is no depth sensor in the
project, so 'distance' here can only be validated against apparent size.
